predecessors.name: Pallava dynasty
predecessors.text: Kolar and its country, the first Ganga capital

successors.name: Chola Empire
successors.text: Gangavadi: the page's territory list is the Mysore, Hassan, Mandya, Ramanagara, Chamarajanagar, Tumkur, Kolar and Bangalore districts

ledger.x: c. 350: Konganivarma Madhava makes Kolar his capital and founds the Western Ganga kingdom. The page says he "made Kolar his capital around 350", ruled about twenty years, and links the founding to Samudragupta's southern campaigns "before 350"; the infobox: "Subordinate to Pallava until 350", "Established 350". The…
390: the Ganga capital moves from Kolar to Talakad.
390: the Ganga rule extends to Talakad.
430: the Gangas consolidate the eastern territories around Bangalore, Kolar and Tumkur.
470: the Gangas gain the Kongu region from the Kalabhra shape.
470: "The Gangas gained control of the Kongu region and other areas".

c. 550: the Gangas become feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas. "The Western Ganga sovereignty lasted from about 350 to 550 CE" and "After the rise of the imperial Chalukyas of Badami, the Gangas accepted Chalukya overlordship and fought for the cause of their overlords against the Pallavas of Kanchi"; "the Gangas were…
753: the Rashtrakutas replace the Badami Chalukyas.
780: Rashtrakuta control of Gangavadi begins under Dhruva.
819 (bridge): the Gangas are Rashtrakuta feudatories after the peace.
998: Rajaraja I of the Cholas annexes Gangapadi.
999: the last Ganga ruler (Rachamalla V, listed 986-999) goes and the Cholas hold Gangavadi.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta conquest of Gangavadi
wars.outcome: The Rashtrakutas under Dhruva (from 780) and Govinda III (793-814) bring Gangavadi under control, an occupation to 819; a Ganga resurgence regains partial control by 819 and Amoghavarsha I makes peace by marrying his daughters to the Gangas, who remain…

wars.name: Chola conquest of Gangapadi
wars.outcome: Rajaraja I annexes Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and Tadigaipadi in 998 and holds the Gangavadi province by 1004.

certainty.note: No border is given for any year; Gangavadi is named by districts and the Kongu region by its cities.
